articles.title: Amazon mistakenly hits AWS users with billion dollar bills
articles.text:
You know the shock that you see when a bill is higher than you thought? Well, some Amazon Web Services (AWS) users just got the bill shock of their lives.
Some AWS users were surprised when they learned their forecasted monthly expenses would be in the billions, with some even hitting the trillion-dollar mark.
Bill Radjewski, the owner-operator of CollegeFootballData.com, posted to X that he woke up to an email from AWS that he had racked up more than US$1.5 billion (approx. C$2.1 billion) in usage fees, and told Wired that his August 1 bill was on pace to cost him more than US$3 billion (approx. C$4.2 billion).
Radjewski also noted to Wired in an email that over the six-plus years he has had the account, his monthly spending was never more than a couple of cents.
And there are other examples, like India-based AI Engineer Bharath, who noted on X “my soul left my body” after seeing a US$1.5 trillion (approx C$2.1 trillion) bill on their AWS account.
Now, the good news is that this was a glitch, and no one is actually racking up a trillion-dollar AWS bill overnight. Most of the people publicly sharing their AWS bills haven’t spent more than a dollar per month on the service.
AWS’ support team wrote on social media that “We are investigating issues with Cost Explorer reflecting inaccurate estimated billing data,” noting in a reply that “There are no customer actions required at this time.”
Moreover, it looks like the issue might already be fixed. AWS noted on the service health dashboard that a faulty configuration change within the billing system was implemented on July 16. The company noted “this system relies on unit conversion data to calculate line item charges,” and that the change “caused updates to the unit conversion data to fail,” which led to the outrageous costs.
Several logs on the health dashboard showed that AWS tried multiple fixes across two days before finally marking the issue as fully resolved.

articles.title: ‘I haven’t seen a thinner laptop than this’: Lenovo’s new Yoga is a marvel of minimalism — and that’s not even the best thing about it
articles.text:
TechRadar Verdict
The Lenovo Yoga Slim 7x Gen 11 impresses in many areas. Despite being super thin, its construction feels premium and solid. Its performance is also strong in numerous areas, thanks to the new Snapdragon X2 Elite chip. The display is also great, if a little reflective at times, and the battery life is among the best in this sector. It might lack the port selection of its rivals, and it’s not exactly cheap, but the Yoga Slim 7x Gen 11 is still a good choice for those who want a good balance between power and portability.
Pros
- +Brilliant build quality 
- +Ultra thin 
- +Long battery life 
Cons
- -Heats up under stress 
- -Key strokes are a little heavy 
- -Fewer ports than some rivals 
Why you can trust TechRadar
Lenovo Yoga Slim 7x Gen 11: Two-minute review
The Lenovo Yoga Slim 7x Gen 11 is an ultra-thin laptop with a strong spec that makes it more than capable for workday use.
It looks smart, thanks to its minimalist form. All sides are flat, and the Cosmic Blue colorway is subtle yet helps to distinguish it in this largely monochromatic sector.
The build quality is excellent. The body is as premium as it comes, feeling very solid but also light and smooth to the touch. In fact, it could probably lay claim to having one of the best laptop constructions around right now. Allied to that lightness is its thinness, which is quite remarkable, although the thick rear foot underneath somewhat negates this aspect, which is a shame. What’s more, these truncated dimensions mean that you get three ports, all of which are USB-C.
With the new Snapdragon X2 Elite chip equipped, the Yoga Slim 7x Gen 11 is a capable all-round performer. It handles multiple browser tabs and 4K streaming with ease, as well as basic productivity. While it's not necessarily aimed at gamers and lacks a dedicated GPU, it's even capable of some light gaming; it managed to run Cyberpunk 2077 in a playable state, although don't expect top-tier performance. Heat and fan noise are generated when such workloads are conducted, but neither is too disruptive.
Another advantage of the X2 Elite chip is the improved efficiency. This is evident in the battery life of the Yoga Slim 7x Gen 11, which is one of its most impressive aspects. It lasted close to a full day when I ran a movie on a continuous loop, which ranks among the best in class. It’s also quick to charge, taking about two hours to do so.
The 2.8K display in my review unit was sharp, bright, and vivid, although it was prone to showing reflections at times. For the most part, though, these were only apparent in the most unfavorable of lighting conditions.
The keyboard is fairly easy to use, thanks to the ergonomic keycaps and their spacing. However, presses are a little heavier than you might expect, so this can take some getting used to if you’ve come from a board that requires a light touch. The touchpad is large and smooth, which makes for easy navigation, while taps and clicks are responsive and provide good feedback.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
The Yoga Slim 7x Gen 11 commands a reasonably high price tag, but considering its spec and quality, it makes for good value compared to some of its less premium-feeling rivals. It might lack the ports and graphical performance of other laptops, but it’s a fine choice if portability and build quality are among your top priorities.
Lenovo Yoga Slim 7x Gen 11 review: Price & availability
- Starts from $999.99 / £945 / AU$1,999
- Available now in one colorway
- Reasonably expensive for the spec
The Yoga Slim 7x Gen 11 starts from $999.99 / £945 / AU$1,999 and is available now in one color: Cosmic Blue. This base spec features a Snapdragon X2 Plus X2P-42-100, 16GB of RAM, 512GB of storage, and WUXGA display. This isn't exactly cheap, and costs escalate quickly as you move up the model range. The top-spec unit, which features 32GB of RAM, 1TB of storage, and a 2.8K display, costs $2,299.99 (about £1,700 / AU$3,300).
If you’re looking for another thin and light laptop, then the HP OmniBook 7 is a very strong alternative. I was very impressed with its performance when I reviewed it, and its only missteps are the port placements and slightly harsh keyboard. It's base model is slightly cheaper than the Yoga Slim 7x Gen 11's in the US, and significantly so in the UK.
There’s also the Asus Zenbook A14, which is incredibly thin and light, and has one of the best battery lifespans around. However, it lacks the build quality and display brightness of the Yoga Slim 7x Gen 11, yet it’s significantly more expensive when comparing like-for-like models.
- Value score: 4 / 5
Lenovo Yoga Slim 7x Gen 11 review: Specs
| Row 0 - Cell 0 | Base spec | Max spec | 
| Price | $999.99 / £945 / AU$1,999 | $2,299.99 (about £1,700 / AU$3,300) | 
| CPU | Snapdragon X2 Plus X2P-42-100 Processor (4.04 GHz) | Snapdragon X2 Elite X2E-80-100 Processor (4.70 GHz) | 
| Graphics | Integrated | Integrated | 
| RAM | 16GB LPDDR5X | 32GB LPDDR5X | 
| Display | 14-inch WUXGA (1920 x 1200), OLED, Glare, HDR 500 True Black, 100% DCI-P3, 400 nits, 60Hz | 14-inch 2.8K WQXGA+ (2880 x 1800), OLED, Glare, HDR 1000 True Black, 100% DCI-P3, 500 nits, PureSight Pro, 120Hz | 
| Storage | 512GB SSD M.2 PCIe Gen4 | 1TB SSD M.2 PCIe Gen4 | 
| Ports and Connectivity | 3x USB-C (USB4 40Gbps); Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 5.4 | 3x USB-C (USB4 40Gbps); Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 5.4 | 
| Battery | 70Wh | 70Wh | 
| Weight | 2.6lbs (1.2kg) | 2.6lbs (1.2kg) | 
| Dimensions | 12.3 x 8.7 x 0.6 inches / 312 x 221 x 14mm | 12.3 x 8.7 x 0.6 inches / 312 x 221 x 14mm | 
Lenovo Yoga Slim 7x Gen 11 review: Design
- Extremely thin
- Premium materials
- Lacks ports
The minimalist design of the Yoga Slim 7x Gen 11 is appealing, while the dark Cosmic Blue colorway rescues the unit from looking dull. The rounded sides and corners help to soften its appearance. Most sides are flat, with no extraneous bulges, save for the central camera bezel that extends beyond the rest of the lid. However, the overhang this creates actually helps you to open the lid, which is a thoughtful touch.
The body is one of the best I’ve seen in a laptop. It looks and feels premium, rivaling what the best MacBooks have to offer. It’s incredibly smooth and seems very durable. There’s some flex to the base and the lid, but they’re remarkably solid when you consider just how light the whole unit is. The lid is also very stable when open, and adjustments are smooth and easy to make.
Just as impressive is the thinness of the Yoga Slim 7x Gen 11. It’s certainly one of the thinnest 14-inch laptops I’ve seen, although it’s a shame the bulky bar underneath, which acts as the rear foot, somewhat undermines this aspect. This is no doubt to improve airflow from the underside vent, which is more exposed than many others.
To achieve this thinness, port selection has been compromised. There are only three ports, all of which are USB-C, which means you’ll need plenty of adapters (or a hub) if you’re going to be connecting lots of peripherals. The saving grace is that all ports have 40Gbps transfer rates, support the Power Delivery standard, and can be used to charge the laptop itself. They’re also split across both sides of the unit, which improves practicality.
On the right you’ll also find the power button and a button for disabling the webcam, which might disappoint those hoping for a physical privacy shutter.
- Design score: 4 / 5
Lenovo Yoga Slim 7x Gen 11 review: Performance
- Capable everyday performance
- Light gaming possible
- Keys are a little heavy
3DMark: Night Raid: 40,637; Fire Strike: 7,911; Steel Nomad: 1,051; Solar Bay: 21,754; Solar Bay Unlimited: 22,518; Solar Bay Extreme: 2,491; Solar Bay Extreme Unlimited: 2,526
Geekbench 6.5: Multicore: 20,362; Single-core: 3,815
Cinebench R23: Multi Core: 13,071; Cinebench R24: Single Core: 90; Multi Core: 723
Crossmark: Overall: 1,896; Productivity: 1,703; Creativity: 2,171; Responsiveness: 1,742
Passmark Overall: 7,821.2; CPU: 30,341.4; 2D Graphics: 594.2; 3D Graphics: 6,632.9; Memory: 3,429.5; Disk: 51,620.7
BlackMagicDisk: Read: 5,214MB/s; Write: 4,947MB/s
HandBrake 4K to 1080p: 63.68fps
Total War: Warhammer III: 1080p, Medium: 43fps
Total War: Warhammer III: 1800p, Ultra: 11fps
Battery Life (TechRadar movie test): 23 hours and 30 minutes
For everyday use, the Yoga Slim 7x Gen 11 is certainly fast enough. It handled many of the tasks I threw at it with aplomb, from basic productivity to 4K streaming. With the 32GB of RAM in my unit, it also handled multi-tab web browsing with ease.
No doubt a lot of this performance comes from the new Snapdragon X2 Elite chip inside the Yoga Slim 7x Gen 11. Qualcomm claims this chip is a stronger performer than Intel equivalents, and based on our testing this appears to be true. For instance, it beat the Geekbench Single Core benchmark score of the HP OmniBook 7, with its Intel Core 5 220H, by over a thousand points, and doubled its Multi Core score.
When it comes to gaming, the Yoga Slim 7x Gen 11 was less competent, but that's hardly a surprise — it's not really aimed at wooing gamers, given it doesn’t have a dedicated GPU. However, I still managed to run Cyberpunk 2077 in a playable state, albeit with ray tracing disabled and resolution scaling set to Balanced. It wasn’t exactly a smooth experience, so it's not likely to be for you if you're in the market for a dedicated gaming laptop, but if you want a productivity powerhouse with just a little casual gaming on the side, it should suffice.
As expected, the fans can be heard whirring away in such cases, but the noise isn’t too disruptive. Heat is also generated, and temperatures can get quite high in places, although thankfully these hotspots are confined to the top and underside of the base.
The display in my review unit was crisp, thanks to its 2880 x 1800 resolution, and the high levels of brightness ensure content is viewable in most conditions. There were times when reflections showed on screen, but only when the lighting in my environment was particularly unsuitable.
The keys in the Yoga Slim 7x Gen 11 adopt Lenovo’s trademark shape, which are very ergonomic. The generous spacing between them also makes for a forgiving typing experience. However, they’re a little heavier and travel further than you might expect, which might throw off those who prefer a light and snappy response. The touchpad is suitably large and incredibly smooth, making it conducive to cursor navigation. Taps are responsive without being overly sensitive, and clicks are easy to perform and provide plenty of feedback.
- Performance score: 4 / 5
Lenovo Yoga Slim 7x Gen 11 review: Battery life
The battery life of the Yoga Slim 7x Gen 11 is very impressive. No doubt that aforementioned new Snapdragon chip plays a major part here, due to its improved efficiency. It managed to last just under 24 hours in our movie playback test, putting it ahead of many other laptops in this sector. This may be partly due to that aforementioned chipset, which Snapdragon claims brings improved efficiency. Charging is a quick affair, too, as it took about two hours to fully replenish.
However, there are those that can match and even outlast it, such as the HP OmniBook 7, which managed 26 hours in the same test. And then there’s the Asus Zenbook A14, which managed a staggering 28 hours and 25 minutes.
- Battery life score: 4.5 / 5
Should I buy the Lenovo Yoga Slim 7x Gen 11?
Scorecard
| Attributes | Notes | Rating | 
| Value | It seems expensive, but when you consider its design and spec, it’s reasonable. | 4 / 5 | 
| Design | I couldn’t help but marvel at its thin and premium design. The port selection is disappointing, though. | 4 / 5 | 
| Performance | Great for everyday tasks, and it can even handle light gaming. The display is vivid if a little reflective, and it can get hot under load. | 4 / 5 | 
| Battery life | Among the best in class, it really can last a full day. It’s quick to charge, too. | 4.5 / 5 | 
| Total Score | The Yoga Slim 7x Gen 11 is great if you need a thin yet powerful Windows machine that lasts all day unplugged. A few areas are less impressive, but it’s still a good value proposition. | 4 / 5 | 
Buy it if…
You want one of the thinnest laptops around
That bulky foot underneath might spoil things a little, but the Yoga Slim 7x Gen 11 is still incredibly thin.
You want a premium design
It looks premium, and the body feels exquisite and hardwearing. It’s also quite light.
Don't buy it if…
You want lots of ports
There are only three ports on board, and all are USB-C, so you'll need a hub if you have lots of connections to make.
You want light keys
Although they’re comfortable to use, the keys on the Yoga Slim 7x Gen 11 are a little heavier than on many other laptops, which might take some getting used to.
Lenovo Yoga Slim 7x Gen 11 review: Also consider
HP OmniBook 7 14-inch (2025)
Like the Yoga Slim 7x Gen 11, the OmniBook 7 is an incredibly thin and light laptop. Not only that, I was very impressed with how well it handled all kinds of workloads, and it has a superb battery life to boot. Read our full HP OmniBook 7 14-inch (2025) review.
Asus Zenbook A14
Another portable hero, the A14 is even lighter than the Yoga Slim 7x Gen 11. However, its battery life is even better; in fact, it’s the most enduring laptop I’ve ever tested, lasting a staggering 28 hours in our movie playback test. Its build isn’t as premium as the Yoga Slim 7x Gen 11’s, and its display isn’t as bright, but it’s still a capable machine. Read our full Asus Zenbook A14 review.
How I tested the Lenovo Yoga Slim 7x Gen 11
- Tested for several days
- Used for a variety of tasks
- Plentiful laptop experience
I tested the Yoga Slim 7x Gen 11 for several days, during which time I used it for a variety of tasks, from productivity and browsing to streaming and gaming.
I also ran our series of benchmark tests, designed to assess every aspect of a laptop's performance. I also ran a movie on a continuous loop to test the battery life.
I've been using laptops for decades, and have reviewed a large number of them, from small budget models to large gaming machines.

articles.title: Ce champion de l'autonomie des smartphones milieu de gamme perd 130 € jusqu'à ce soir sur Amazon
articles.text:
Realme cherche à bousculer le milieu de gamme avec des smartphones bien équipés à prix contenu. Le Realme 16 Pro en est la preuve : lancé il y a quelques mois, il mise sur une fiche technique solide portée par un capteur photo de 200 Mpx, un écran AMOLED 144 Hz et une batterie de 6 500 mAh. Il tire son épingle du jeu aujourd’hui grâce à une réduction de 130 euros.
Les forces du Realme 16 Pro
- Un écran Amoled lumineux à 144 Hz
- Une batterie de 6 500 mAh pour tenir deux jours
- Un capteur grand-angle de 200 mégapixels
Habituellement vendu 429 euros, le Realme 16 Pro passe aujourd’hui à 299 euros sur Amazon, soit 30 % de remise. Le promo finit ce soir à minuit.
Si, par la suite, l’offre mentionnée dans cet article n’est plus disponible, merci de jeter un coup d’œil ci-dessous afin de dénicher d’autres offres concernant le Realme 16 Pro. Le tableau s’actualise automatiquement.
Un écran lumineux et un format maîtrisé
Realme apporte un soin particulier à l’esthétique de son milieu de gamme. Son dos en verre poli apporte une touche d’élégance, même s’il a tendance à collecter les traces de doigts. Avec 7,75 mm d’épaisseur et 192 grammes sur la balance, le Realme 16 Pro reste agréable en main malgré la taille de son écran. Et grâce à sa certification IP68/IP69K, vous avez un smartphone robuste et résistant à l’eau, à la poussière et aux jets haute pression.
C’est l’un des plus gros atouts de ce téléphone : sa dalle AMOLED de 6,78 pouces jouit d’une belle définition 1,5K (2772 x 1272 pixels) et offre un taux de rafraîchissement grimpant jusqu’à 144 Hz pour une fluidité irréprochable au quotidien. Mais là où le smartphone impressionne vraiment, c’est sur la lisibilité : avec un pic de luminosité maximal de 6 500 nits en HDR, l’affichage reste parfaitement lisible et agréable à consulter, même en plein soleil.
Autonomie XXL et de belles photos de jour
Côté performances, c’est la puce Dimensity 7300 Max de MediaTek qui est à l’action. Elle assure une expérience fluide au quotidien, même si elle montre ses limites dans les jeux les plus exigeants. En revanche, Realme marque des points en proposant 5 ans de mises à jour Android et 6 ans de correctifs de sécurité, un engagement rassurant pour la longévité du smartphone.
C’est clairement sur l’endurance que le Realme 16 Pro marque des points. Sa batterie silicium-carbone de 6 500 mAh permet de tenir environ deux jours en usage mixte, un résultat qui le place parmi les meilleurs du segment. La recharge filaire à 45 W, en revanche, reste un cran en dessous de ce que propose son grand frère, le 16 Pro+, avec ses 80 W. Il faudra aussi se passer de recharge sans fil.
Quant à la photo, on découvre un capteur principal de 200 Mpx avec stabilisation optique et un ultra-grand-angle de 8 Mpx. Malgré un équipement photo minimaliste, le Realme 16 Pro assure une bonne polyvalence. Et les photos qu’il réalise offrent une qualité satisfaisante, de jour comme de nuit.
Si vous souhaitez en savoir plus sur ce smartphone, nous vous conseillons de lire notre test du Realme 16 Pro.
Si vous cherchez à comparer ce modèle avec d’autres références du segment, vous pouvez consulter notre guide des meilleurs smartphones du moment.

articles.title: Microsoft va tuer son application Whiteboard si vous l’utilisez avec un compte personnel
articles.text:
Si vous utilisez Microsoft Whiteboard avec un compte personnel, préparez-vous. Microsoft vient d’annoncer que son application de tableau blanc, serait prochainement retirée.
Lancé en 2018, Microsoft Whiteboard est un tableau blanc numérique collaboratif conçu pour faciliter le brainstorming, la prise de note et le travail en équipe. La fin de son support ne concerne toutefois pas tout le monde.
Car si Microsoft va cesser de proposer son outil aux utilisateurs avec un compte personnel, Microsoft Whiteboard sera toujours accessible aux utilisateurs professionnels disposant d’un compte payant.
Microsoft Whiteboard accessible uniquement pour les pro
L’annonce de la fin de Microsoft Whiteboard pour les comptes personnels n’a pas vraiment été officialisée par Microsoft. Du moins, pas dans les règles de l’art. La firme de Redmond s’est en effet contentée de n’afficher qu’une simple alerte dans un pop-up à la connexion à Microsoft Whiteboard.
« À compter du 22 août 2026, vous ne pourrez plus créer ni modifier de tableaux blancs. Toutefois, vous pouvez continuer à les afficher et à les exporter jusqu’au 5 septembre 2026, après quoi ils seront définitivement supprimés. » explique ainsi Microsoft tout en renvoyant vers une page censée expliquer comment exporter ceux-ci, mais qui propose en réalité un tutoriel de prise en main de l’outil.
Sur Reddit, les utilisateurs de Microsoft Whiteboard s’interrogent de cette nouvelle qui arrive comme un cheveu sur la soupe.
Microsoft Whiteboard ne disparaît en réalité pas complètement. Celui-ci ne sera plus accessibles pour les utilisateurs ne disposant que d’un compte Microsoft personnel, mais la firme de Redmond continuera de le proposer à ses utilisateurs professionnels.
Une migration technique d’Azure vers OneDrive en cause
A priori, l’abandon de Microsoft Whiteboard pour les comptes personnels serait dû à un changement technique opéré du côté de Microsoft. L’entreprise abandonne progressivement le stockage Azure pour Whiteboard au profit de OneDrive, notamment pour des raisons de sécurité. Les comptes personnels utilisant encore cet ancien stockage Azure, et Microsoft ayant prévu de faire évoluer son produit en le recentrant sur OneDrive for business, la prise en charge de l’application pour les comptes personnels est de fait compromise.

articles.title: Reconditionné vs occasion : comment refurbed garantit des produits tech fiables jusqu'à 40 % moins chers
articles.text:
Ces derniers temps, acheter un smartphone neuf est devenu un luxe. En raison de la crise de RAM et de la hausse du prix des composants, les constructeurs se voient aujourd’hui dans l’obligation de faire grimper la facture. Dans ces conditions, le marché de la seconde main explose, et les produits tech ne font pas exception à la règle. Mais comment s’assurer d’acheter un smartphone sans avoir de mauvaises surprises ?
C’est justement la promesse du reconditionné et du site refurbed, qui s’assure que les produits mis en vente sur son site proposent les mêmes performances que du neuf. Smartphones, PC, consoles de jeu : on en trouve pour tous les prix et tous les usages.
Reconditionné ou d’occasion : quelle est la différence ?
L’achat d’occasion et le reconditionné, s’ils concernent tous les deux le marché de la seconde main, n’ont rien à voir l’un avec l’autre.
L’achat d’un appareil d’occasion entre particuliers s’effectue systématiquement en l’état (qu’il soit bon ou mauvais) et en prenant le risque que, finalement, une fois de retour chez vous, l’appareil ne fonctionne pas. Le marché du reconditionné s’appuie, lui, sur un circuit professionnel.
Un produit reconditionné n’est pas simplement revendu : il est pris en charge par un vendeur qualifié avant sa remise sur le marché. Le matériel subit d’abord une série de tests pour évaluer ses fonctionnalités techniques. Il est ensuite nettoyé, puis restauré si des réparations ou le remplacement de composants s’avèrent nécessaires.
C’est ce processus de contrôle qualité et de remise en état qui différencie le reconditionné du simple marché de l’occasion entre particuliers. En passant par le reconditionné comme chez refurbed, vous vous assurez que l’appareil a déjà été vérifié et vous avez la garantie qu’il fonctionne parfaitement une fois que vous l’aurez reçu.
Le reconditionné : économique et écologique
Les chiffres parlent d’eux-mêmes. En 2025, 12 % des achats de smartphones se faisaient en passant par le reconditionné contre 10 % pour les achats d’occasion entre particuliers. Un écart qui s’explique notamment par la sécurité qu’apporte le recours à un professionnel.
Toujours selon l’Insee, le prix est le premier critère de choix pour 76 % des personnes interrogées. Avec des tarifs jusqu’à 40 % en dessous des prix du neuf, les enseignes de produits reconditionnés comme refurbed offrent une option abordable sur le marché des produits tech.
Autre argument important pour le consommateur : l’environnement. Acheter un produit reconditionné est un moyen de limiter les déchets électroniques en prolongeant la durée de vie d’un produit, et limite par là même occasion l’extraction de nouvelles matières premières pour fabriquer un produit neuf.
Pour chiffrer cet impact, refurbed a développé une application web qui permet de calculer l’empreinte environnementale des smartphones, des tablettes et des ordinateurs portables reconditionnés, et de la comparer de façon transparente à celle de leurs équivalents neufs. refurbed a pris soin de développer son application Product Footprint App en partenariat avec Fraunhofer Austria, l’un des principaux instituts de recherche européens.
Le modèle de calcul disponible via l’app est ainsi certifié ISO 14040 et ISO 14044, gage de sérieux.
refurbed, du reconditionné depuis 2017
Fondée il y a bientôt 10 ans, l’entreprise autrichienne refurbed est présente sur 24 marchés à travers l’Europe et propose aujourd’hui plus de 65 000 références sur son site web. Presque tous les univers de l’électronique sont représentés : des smartphones aux tablettes en passant par les ordinateurs, les consoles de jeux et le petit électroménager.
Le fonctionnement de la plateforme est assez simple : les différents produits sont proposés par des revendeurs, et refurbed fait office de market place. L’entreprise met ainsi en relation vendeurs et acheteurs.
Mais ce n’est pas tout. Pour s’assurer que chaque acheteur soit pleinement satisfait de son achat, refurbed propose un suivi très rigoureux des vendeurs de sa plateforme. La qualité du matériel fourni, la fiabilité des livraisons et la satisfaction client sont régulièrement contrôlées de différentes façons. L’une d’elles consiste à réaliser des achats tests et identifier tout dysfonctionnement, que ce soit sur le parcours d’achat ou sur la qualité du produit reçu.
Enfin, pour les utilisateurs recherchant un matériel sans altération d’usage, la plateforme intègre un grade Premium. Les références classées dans cette catégorie sont certifiées techniquement et visuellement identiques à des modèles neufs.

articles.title: Yelp Unifies ML Model Training with Training Orchestrator
articles.text:
Yelp has launched Training Orchestrator. This new internal framework replaces individual team Spark training scripts. Now, it uses a configuration-driven, DAG-based execution model. The move tackles a common problem in large ML platforms. Each applied ML team created its own orchestration. This led to duplicated code, inconsistent configurations, and fragile custom monitoring.
Training at Yelp previously ran as monolithic scripts tightly coupled to Spark cluster and job-launcher execution. That coupling caused no local runs, poor testability, and slow iteration. A small code change needed submitting a Spark job. Then, you had to wait for containers and clusters to start up before finding out if there was a failure. Validation logic was spread out in scripts. This made it difficult to reproduce past runs in different environments. There were issues with inconsistent settings and missing provenance.
Training Orchestrator separates what to run from how it runs. Pipelines use Pydantic-based configuration objects. These include an orchestrator config, an MLflow run config, and various step configs. All are validated when created, so no compute is wasted. The orchestrator uses declared step dependencies to create a Directed Acyclic Graph. It then runs the steps in topological order. A shared Spark/MLflow context is added, allowing the same step definitions to run unchanged, whether locally, in Jupyter, or in production. Each step links a settings class to a user-defined function. It uses an input/output schema to show what it takes and gives back. For example, a PrepareDataStep takes in a dataset and outputs a prepared dataset. This setup lets teams easily change preprocessing logic. They can run different model versions simultaneously. Moreover, they can reuse functions across pipelines without changing orchestration code.
Schema validation quickly catches configuration mismatches. It flags issues like incorrect step input/output pairings and out-of-range parameters in seconds. This is much faster than finding them hours into a running Spark job. Developers can run full pipelines locally with sample data since steps are separate from infrastructure. They can also write unit tests for each step. Plus, caching input for data-loading steps reduces integration test time on smaller data sets. Every run's complete configuration is logged automatically as an MLflow artifact, making reruns replayable from that single record. Slack notifications and MLflow run tracking, previously hand-rolled per team, now require only a few configuration parameters.
The Training Orchestrator works with Yelp's ML platform. It connects feature stores, a shared neural network, a gradient-boosted-tree library, and MLflow for tracking and deployment. The Core Machine Learning Team sees it as the vital orchestration layer they needed. It is an internal framework, not an open-source release. Yelp plans to add clear steps for model evaluation, comparison, and explanation. It will also implement lineage tracking at the orchestration layer. This way, it will spread to current pipelines without needing migration.
The main pattern involves Pydantic-validated, declarative step configs that drive a DAG execution engine. This pattern separates training logic from cluster runtime. It also enables local runs and unit testing. This approach can be used beyond Yelp's Spark-specific stack. The tradeoff involves an initial investment in schema and step-type design. It also requires migrating existing scripts into the settings-and-function contract. Yelp views this as a way to centralise the cost, so teams don’t have to pay it repeatedly.
Yelp's effort reflects a wider trend in the industry. Many companies with several ML teams are moving towards a centralised, clear training infrastructure. Netflix has also moved forward with Metaflow. They recently added a configuration object. This lets teams manage flow behaviour clearly across the many ML pipelines they maintain. Uber's Michelangelo platform was created to tackle the fragmentation issue that Yelp mentions. It helps teams using different tools by providing a clear path from prototyping to production.
These efforts show a shared conclusion from various engineering groups: as more models and training teams emerge, ad hoc orchestration becomes a bottleneck. Centralising this process, despite upfront costs, improves reproducibility, testability, and developer speed.

articles.title: Android Auto ajoute enfin le compteur de vitesse à Google Maps, mais sûrement pas pour vous
articles.text:
Android Auto ajoute enfin le compteur de vitesse à Google Maps, mais sûrement pas pour vous
Google Maps commence enfin à afficher le compteur de vitesse sur Android Auto. La fonctionnalité est cependant en cours de peaufinage, sa disponibilité restant limitée à quelques conducteurs bien spécifiques.
La version de Google Maps sur Android Auto a l’avantage d’offrir un affichage adapté aux grands écrans de nos habitacles, mais oublie au passage quelques fonctionnalités. Le compteur de vitesse, rappel plus qu’utile aux côtés des limitations, en fait d’ailleurs partie. Une faiblesse qui commence enfin à disparaitre chez certains utilisateurs ayant installé la version bêta de l’application GPS.
Fini les excès de vitesse avec Google Maps ? Google donne cet avantage clé jusqu’alors réservé à Waze
S'il a fallu un temps considérable à Google Maps pour intégrer l'affichage des limitations de vitesse, l'attente a été encore plus longue pour voir apparaître le compteur de vitesse en temps réel sur Android Auto. C’est d'autant plus frustrant quand on sait que Google a déployé cette fonctionnalité sur Apple CarPlay dès juillet 2024, et qu'elle existe sur smartphones depuis longtemps.
Aujourd'hui, la situation se débloque enfin. Quelques utilisateurs d'Android Auto ont récemment signalé sur Reddit l'apparition de ce fameux compteur directement sur l'écran de leur véhicule. Une très bonne nouvelle qui est à tempérer, étant donné que le déploiement reste extrêmement restreint. Le principal témoignage provient en effet d'un automobiliste canadien qui utilise la version bêta n°26.29.02.946673643 de l'application de navigation.
Google en est donc à une phase de test très ciblée, suggérant encore quelques semaines d'attente avant un déploiement en version finale chez tous les utilisateurs de Maps. On espère quand même que cela ne prendra pas des mois, comme c’est parfois le cas avec certaines mises à jour d'Android Auto.
En attendant, vous pouvez toujours utiliser une alternative de la firme américaine rachetée en 2013 : Waze. L’application de GPS communautaire propose en effet le compteur de vitesse depuis des années (couplé aux limitations), que ce soit sur smartphone, Android Auto ou CarPlay.
Waze - GPS, Maps & Traffic
Waze est le GPS communautaire de référence, il vous permet d’établir un itinéraire et une navigation en connaissant le trafic et les dangers de la route. L'application ultime pour les conducteurs !

articles.title: Doodle de Google para hoy 20 de julio celebra la independencia de Colombia
articles.text:
Como parte de la tradición de Google, este 20 de julio el buscador se viste en homenaje a la independencia de Colombia. Para este año, en la página de inicio el diseño muestra la bandera tricolor del país ondeando en el cielo.
Este gesto es solo visible accediendo al buscador desde Colombia y estará activo durante todo este lunes, como parte de la conmemoración del grito de independencia de 1810, que marcó el inicio de una lucha interna para desprenderse del Virreinato de la Nueva Granada y empezar la organización de una nueva nación, que posteriormente terminaría con el establecimiento de la Gran Colombia.
PUBLICIDAD
Cómo es el doodle de Google para el 20 de julio de 2026
A diferencia de otros años, Google volvió a utilizar el diseño que vimos en 2025. Al abrir la página de inicio del buscador veremos la bandera de Colombia ondeando en medio de un cielo azul y las letras de Google en forma de nube. En algunos casos, el azul tiene un tono oscuro y en otros, claro.
En la página oficial no hay ninguna referencia al autor de este diseño de 2025, pero sí una corta reseña del significado de esta fecha:
PUBLICIDAD
“¡Este Doodle anual celebra el Día de la Independencia de Colombia! Un día como hoy, en 1810, los ciudadanos de Bogotá salieron a las calles para protestar contra el dominio español. La fecha se convirtió en día festivo oficial en 1872 y, desde entonces, sirve para conmemorar la libertad, los logros y el progreso de Colombia".
Google también destaca la manera en la que se festeja este día en el país, contando que “los colombianos participan en animadas celebraciones por todo el país, en ciudades como Bogotá, Medellín, Cali, Cartagena y otras. Los desfiles, los eventos culturales y las manifestaciones de orgullo nacional son muy habituales en esta festividad”.
PUBLICIDAD
Además del Doodle de la página de inicio, Google da información histórica de esta fecha al hacer clic sobre la ilustración. Se abre una búsqueda con datos importantes sobre lo que se debe saber sobre este día y noticias relevantes sobre los festejos y desfiles que se organizan en las diferentes ciudades del país.
Finalmente, el logo del buscador también hizo un ligero cambio durante el día en cada búsqueda que se realice en la página, quitando las letras ‘O’ de Google para poner la bandera de Colombia.
PUBLICIDAD
Cómo usar Google Maps para ver los cierres víales del 20 de julio en Colombia
Las celebraciones del Día de la Independencia en Colombia este 20 de julio de 2026 traen consigo desfiles militares y actos cívicos en ciudades como Bogotá, Medellín, Cali y Barranquilla, lo que provoca numerosos cierres viales y desvíos. Esta situación complica la movilidad y exige a los ciudadanos una planificación cuidadosa de sus desplazamientos.
En este contexto, Google Maps es una herramienta esencial para evitar contratiempos en el tráfico. Permite consultar en tiempo real el estado de las vías y anticipar embotellamientos, optimizando el trayecto hacia el destino deseado.
PUBLICIDAD
Usar Google Maps es sencillo: se debe abrir la aplicación o acceder desde el navegador, centrar el mapa en la ciudad y zona de interés y activar la capa de tráfico tocando el ícono correspondiente, normalmente en la esquina superior derecha.
Al activar esta función, el mapa despliega líneas de colores: verde para tráfico fluido, naranja o amarillo para congestión moderada, rojo para tráfico lento y rojo oscuro donde la circulación está prácticamente detenida. Los cierres oficiales, típicos en los recorridos de los desfiles, aparecen como círculos rojos con una línea blanca, mientras que las vías intransitables muestran el símbolo de “Dirección prohibida”.
PUBLICIDAD
Consultar Google Maps justo antes de salir es clave, ya que el tráfico puede cambiar cada 15 minutos debido a ajustes en los desvíos y la afluencia de vehículos. La aplicación actualiza las rutas en función de la congestión, facilitando la elección de caminos alternativos para evitar demoras.
PUBLICIDAD
PUBLICIDAD

articles.title: Edge of Eternity Studio Shut Down Ahead of Sequel Launch
articles.text: Amid mass layoffs at Xbox and studio closures elsewhere, more bad news emerges from the ailing gaming industry, as Midgar, the Nacon-owned studio behind Edge of Eternity, a turn-based JRPG adventure game, has officially announced that it would be shutting down. Earlier this year, Nacon also shut down Spiders, the studio behind GreedFall, for similar reasons . Similarly, Nacon also went on to publish a GreedFall DLC after the studio shut down. The closure comes as a result of a court-ordered liquidation, which follows the studio's failure to find a buyer. The announcement comes by way of a LinkedIn post by the studio's co-founder and current Nacon CTO, Jérémy Zeler-Maury, who says that "we worked until the very end to find a solution that could preserve both the company and the team," but after exhausting other alternatives, this is the only way forward. articles.title: Garmin se lanza a la yugular de las Whoop y Fitbit Air con Cirqa, su pulsera inteligente sin pantalla ni suscripción
articles.text:
El segmento de las pulseras inteligentes acaba de sumar a un nuevo jugador de peso. Garmin ha presentado Cirqa, su propia versión de este tipo de wearables para competir con Whoop y Fitbit Air, los principales exponentes del mercado. Y lo más interesante de todo es que no requiere de una suscripción para funcionar.
En lo que respecta a diseño y funcionalidades, la Garmin Cirqa no se diferencia demasiado de lo que ya ofrecen sus rivales. Es un dispositivo sencillo y con un diseño minimalista que permite que la correa pase desapercibida y se amolde a cualquier tipo de uso e indumentaria.
Garmin ha dotado a su pulsera inteligente Cirqa de un módulo que incluye todos los sensores necesarios para el monitoreo físico y de salud. El nuevo dispositivo puede registrar más de 80 tipos de actividades físicas y deportivas, y brinda seguimiento de ritmo cardíaco, nivel de oxígeno en sangre, calidad del sueño, calorías quemadas, niveles de estrés, temperatura de la piel y más.
Como no podía ser de otra manera, toda la información que recopila el aparato se sincroniza y visualiza a través de Garmin Connect. Dicha app está disponible tanto en iPhone como en Android. Esto permite acceder a reportes detallados, gráficos y toda la información necesaria para llevar un seguimiento pormenorizado del estado físico.
Garmin Cirqa, la pulsera inteligente que compite con Whoop y Fitbit Air
Si bien Garmin Cirqa guarda un importante parecido estético con las pulseras de Whoop y la Fitbit Air de Google, sí tiene una diferencia importante. El nuevo producto de Garmin incluye un botón físico al costado del módulo de sensores, cuando los modelos de la competencia no tienen ningún tipo de control de este tipo.
La tecla incluida en Garmin Cirqa permite cambiar entre las actividades físicas favoritas, sin necesidad de sacar el móvil del bolsillo. Su ubicación promete no generar molestias ni incomodidad a los usuarios. En lo que respecta a la autonomía, el wearable está equipado con una batería que promete una duración de hasta 10 días con una carga.
Uno de los puntos atractivos de Garmin Cirqa es que no requiere de una suscripción para funcionar. Esto la convierte de inmediato en una alternativa bastante atractiva a la Whoop 5.0, que obligatoriamente requiere la contratación de un plan de pago. Y si bien el nuevo dispositivo es más caro que la Fitbit Air, Google también requiere de una suscripción a Health Premium para acceder a características adicionales.
La pulsera inteligente Garmin Cirqa se podrá reservar a partir de este viernes 24 de julio, con un precio de 199,99 dólares. El dispositivo estará disponible con dos tamaños de correas: S-M (para circunferencias de muñeca de entre 120 y 200 mm) y L-XL (145 a 240 mm). Las bandas se consiguen en cuatro colores: negro, azul, gris francés y malva.

articles.title: What to know about the landmark Warner Bros. Discovery sale | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Earlier this year, the streaming and entertainment industry witnessed one of its most high-stakes megadeals ever, stunning industry observers. Not only is it historic in its size, but it is also predicted to disrupt Hollywood and the media business as we know it.
After years of Warner Bros. Discovery struggling under the weight of billions of dollars in debt, compounded by declining cable viewership and fierce competition from streaming platforms, the company has been considering major strategic changes, including selling its entertainment assets to one of its rivals.
Several major players saw the potential in acquiring the media giant, and in December, Netflix announced it would acquire WBD’s studios and streaming for $82.7 billion.
But in a surprise eleventh-hour move in late February, the David Ellison-run Paramount became the winner of this bidding war, offering $111 billion to acquire all of Warner Bros. Discovery’s assets, including its studios, HBO, streaming platforms, games, and TV networks such as CNN and HGTV. Paramount was itself recently acquired by Ellison with significant support from his father, Larry Ellison — the Oracle chairman, world’s sixth-richest person, and major Trump donor.
Paramount’s offer was approved the U.S. Department of Justice (DOJ) in June. However, a federal judge just paused the deal after a lawsuit was filed on July 13 by a coalition of 12 state attorneys general.
Let’s break down exactly what is happening, what’s at stake, and what could come next.
What has happened so far?
This all started back in October when Warner Bros. Discovery (WBD) revealed it was exploring a potential sale after receiving unsolicited interest from several major players in the industry.
The bidding process quickly became competitive, and Paramount and Comcast emerged as serious contenders, with Paramount initially viewed as the frontrunner.
However, WBD’s board eventually determined that an offer from the streaming giant Netflix was the most attractive. Netflix offered $82.7 billion for just Warner’s film, television, and streaming assets.
Thus began the bidding war. Paramount believed its bid, of approximately $108 billion for all of Warner’s assets, was superior to Netflix’s offer that focused on just the studios and streaming. To sweeten its deal, Netflix amended its agreement in January to an all-cash offer at $27.75 per share of Warner Bros. Discovery, further reassuring investors and paving the way for the deal to proceed.
Paramount persisted in its attempts to acquire WBD. Still, the Warner board repeatedly rejected its offers, citing concerns about Paramount’s heavy debt load and the increased risk associated with its proposal, including concern over the suite of investors bankrolling Paramount’s bid, which includes Saudi, Qatari, and Abu Dhabi sovereign wealth funds. The board noted that Paramount’s offer would have left the combined company burdened with $87 billion in debt, a risk they were unwilling to take at the time.
In January, Paramount filed a lawsuit seeking more information about the Netflix deal. A month later, the company sought to sweeten its deal by announcing it would offer a $0.25 per share “ticking fee” to WBD shareholders for each quarter the deal fails to close by December 31, 2026. It also said it would pay the $2.8 billion breakup fee if Warner backs out of its deal with Netflix.
Then, in a final attempt to secure a deal, Paramount increased its offer to $31 per share in February. This prompted the WBD board to prolong discussions with Paramount regarding a potential agreement, considering it as a superior offer. Netflix declined to increase its bid and withdrew from the negotiations.
“The transaction we negotiated would have created shareholder value with a clear path to regulatory approval,” Netflix co-CEOs Ted Sarandos and Greg Peters said in a statement on February 26. “However, we’ve always been disciplined, and at the price required to match Paramount Skydance’s latest offer, the deal is no longer financially attractive, so we are declining to match the Paramount Skydance bid.”
In addition to the billions Paramount already holds in debt, the company is also set to assume the approximately $33 billion in debt Warner Bros. Discovery holds under the agreement. The deal will be backed by a $54 billion debt commitment from Bank of America, Merrill Lynch, Citi, and Apollo Global Management, as well as $45.7 billion in equity from Larry Ellison.
Regulatory hurdles and other concerns
In addition to the assumption of substantial debt posing a significant financial burden, Paramount faces several other hurdles in its deal with WBD that could impact the success of the transaction.
For one, Ellison has warned about significant job reductions that are expected in the near future. There have already been widespread concerns among critics about potential job losses and lower wages.
Ellison is also a controversial figure in the industry, and his ownership of CBS News has been seen as sympathetic and supportive of the administration of Donald Trump, of whom his father, Larry Ellison, is a major donor. Under Ellison’s ownership of Paramount, reporting critical of the administration has been shelved or received increased scrutiny from Ellison or his appointed head of CBS News, the conservative provocateur Bari Weiss.
This has led to some concern among employees at Warner-owned CNN. Trump has personally sought concessions from news divisions critical of him, including a $16 million settlement from CBS, before his FCC would approve the Ellison takeover of Paramount. Before Netflix bowed out of the deal, Trump pressured the company to fire the former Biden White House official Susan Rice from its board. He has publicly stated his intentions to bring CNN to heel under new owners.
Regulatory scrutiny is another hurdle. Such a large-scale merger has attracted attention from lawmakers.
For instance, California Attorney General Rob Bonta said in a statement on February 26 that “these two Hollywood titans have not cleared regulatory scrutiny — the California Department of Justice has an open investigation, and we intend to be vigorous in our review.”
A day before Netflix backed out, it was revealed that a coalition of 11 state attorneys general urged the U.S. Department of Justice (DOJ) to review the merger under concerns it will stifle competition and increase subscription prices. This comes months after U.S. senators Elizabeth Warren, Bernie Sanders, and Richard Blumenthal voiced their concerns to the Justice Department’s Antitrust Division, warning that such a massive merger could have serious consequences for consumers and the industry at large. The senators argue that the merger could give the new media giant excessive market power, enabling it to raise prices for consumers and stifle competition.
Despite the DOJ approving the deal in June, a coalition of 12 state attorneys general filed a lawsuit on July 13 to block the merger. The suit argues it would lessen competition and harm movie theaters, cable distributors, and viewers. The coalition is led by Bonta, with Arizona, Colorado, Connecticut, Massachusetts, Minnesota, Nevada, New Jersey, New Mexico, New York, Oregon, and Washington also joining.
In response, U.S. District Judge Araceli Martínez-Olguín issued a 14-day pause. 
When is the deal expected to close?
Paramount initially aimed to finalize its acquisition of WBD as early as July. However, the transaction has now been temporarily paused until August 3, with a hearing set to assess whether the freeze will extend further.
Stay tuned…

articles.title: Sicherheitsrisiko Overthinking: Diese manipulierten Prompts zwingen KI-Modelle in die Knie
articles.text:
Overthinking bei KI: Wie manipulierte Prompts zur Sicherheitslücke werden
Bei uns Menschen spricht man vom Grübeln oder neudeutsch Overthinking: Das endlose Nachdenken über Probleme, das ständige Abwägen von Konsequenzen, an dessen Ende in den meisten Fällen keine Lösung oder Entscheidung steht, sondern vor allem Erschöpfung. Dieses scheinbar allzu menschliche Phänomen lässt sich auch bei künstlicher Intelligenz beobachten – wenn man ihr nur die richtigen – beziehungsweise bewusst die falschen – Fragen stellt.
Large Reasoning Models und Overthinking
Wie das funktioniert, zeigen Forschende der Zhejiang-Universität im chinesischen Hangzhou. Die noch nicht von unabhängigen Expertinnen und Experten geprüfte Studie hat das Team Anfang Juli auf der International Conference on Machine Learning vorgestellt. „Large Reasoning Models neigen dazu, ‚zu viel nachzudenken“. Das heißt, sie erzeugen übermäßig lange und redundante Argumentationsketten, wenn sie mit unvollständigen oder logisch inkonsistenten Eingaben konfrontiert werden“, heißt es darin.
Als Large Reasoning Models (LRM) werden große Sprachmodelle wie GPT o3, Deepseek R1 und Alibabas Qwen3 bezeichnet, die Anfragen in mehrere logische Teilschritte zerlegen (Chain of Thought) und ihren Denkprozess gleichzeitig transparent machen. Sie gelten als besonders geeignet für komplexe Problemlösungen, etwa bei Mathematikaufgaben oder beim Programmieren. Doch genau diese Arbeitsweise lässt sich von Angreifern missbrauchen.
Komplexe Denkschleifen: Die Forscher „züchten“ Grübel-Prompts
Die chinesischen Forscher haben die Reasoning-Modelle ausgetrickst, indem sie gezielt logisch inkonsistente oder unvollständige Prompts erstellten, die die Modelle in endlose Denkschleifen zwangen. „Die Kernidee besteht darin, die diesen Modellen innewohnende Schwäche des Overthinking auszunutzen, indem die gesamte Gedankengangkette eines Problems automatisch zerlegt wird“ , schreiben sie.
Ihre Methode bezeichnen sie als „hierarchischen genetischen Algorithmus (HGA)“. Dieser bewertet anhand der Antworten des Sprachmodells, welche Eingaben es am ehesten zum Grübeln bringt. Das lässt sich anhand der Antwortlänge aber auch anhand von Schlüsselwörtern wie „aber“, „warte“, „vielleicht“ in der internen Gedankenkette feststellen.
Der HGA fügt immer wieder Mutationen in die Prompts ein. Jene Prompts, die die längsten und komplexesten Denkschleifen auslösen, werden für die nächste Generation beibehalten. Die Forscher „züchten“ sich also vereinfacht gesagt jene Eingaben, die das Sprachmodell am meisten überlasten.
Frühere Studien hatten bereits gezeigt, dass Sprachmodelle in Denkschleifen geraten, wenn die Eingabe entscheidende Informationen unterschlägt, etwa bei der Frage, wie weit eine Person, die 10 Kilometer am Tag wandert insgesamt gelaufen ist, ohne zu erwähnen, wie viele Tage sie insgesamt unterwegs war. Auch das Vertauschen von einer Frage mit dem Text einer anderen Aufgabe oder die fehlende Definition von Variablen in Matheaufgaben bringen die Systeme dazu, immer weiter nachzudenken.
KI-Modelle im Test
Für die Studie hat das Team vier Reasoning Modelle getestet: DeepSeek-R1, Qwen3-Thinking, GPT-o3 und Gemini-2.5-Flash. Die Modelle sollten unter anderem 960 Aufgaben des MATH-Benchmarks lösen, aber eben mit bewusst veränderten Prompts. Das Ergebnis: In einigen Fällen erzeugten die Modelle Antworten, die 26 mal so lang waren wie bei den richtig formulierten Aufgaben. Auch bei Programmier- und Dialogaufgaben stieg die Anzahl der Token, die für die Antwort generiert wurden.
Höherer Tokenverbrauch und Risiko für Serversicherheit
Warum ist das problematisch? Erstens bedeuten mehr Token einen höheren Energie- und Ressourcenverbrauch: Je länger sie überlegen und je länger ihre Antwort, desto mehr Rechenpower und Strom benötigen sie. Vorherige Studien zu Overhinking von KI-Agenten haben gezeigt, dass dadurch die Leistung des Modells insgesamt sinken kann – bei gleichzeitig steigenden Kosten für die Betreiber.
Zweitens bietet das Overthinking einen neuen Angriffsvektor. Angreifer könnten mit den manipulierten Prompts versuchen, die Server der Anbieter in die Knie zu zwingen, ähnlich wie bei einem Distributed-Denial-of-Service (DDoS) Angriff auf Websites. Wenn diese Angriffe in großem Maßstab durchgeführt werden, verschlechtert sich die Servicequalität für alle anderen Nutzenden. Da die bösartige Prompts auf günstigeren Modellen entwickelt und dann erfolgreich auf teure kommerzielle Systeme angewandt werden können, wären großflächige Angriffe prinzipiell denkbar.
Die Forscher fordern deshalb mehr Bewusstsein für diese Art von Angriffen: „Unsere Ergebnisse unterstreichen die Notwendigkeit neuer Verteidigungsparadigmen – wie beispielsweise die bessere Überwachung von Denkschleifen und mehr Robustheit gegenüber logisch inkonsistenten Eingaben“, schreiben sie.
… so wie wie früher die allerersten Taschenrechner, bei denen man nach „dividieren durch Null“ allerschleunigst die Stromquelle kappen mußte, sonst waren die Dinger unrettbar kapu

articles.title: Judge pauses Paramount Warner Bros. acquisition over competition concerns
articles.text:
U.S. District Judge Araceli Martínez-Olguín ordered Paramount Skydance to pause its acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery through August 3 after several U.S. states argued the merger would harm competition.
Martínez-Olguín said the group of states, which included California, New York, Colorado, and others, made a “strong showing” that the merger would decrease competition.
A hearing on August 3 will determine whether the deal should be delayed throughout the course of the lawsuit, according to Reuters.
A coalition of 12 states sued earlier this month, arguing the massive US$110 billion (roughly C$154.7 billion) acquisition would create a media giant with the power to raise prices across film and television.
However, Paramount maintains that the states’ arguments are “without merit,” Martínez-Olguín says the deal looks likely to violate antitrust law.
Further, the merger has far-reaching implications that extend beyond the U.S. Canada’s Competition Bureau is analyzing the acquisition, as Warner Bros. has extensive business in Canada. That includes shooting many of its shows here, including The Last of Us and the ‘Arrowverse’ DC titles like Arrow and The Flash.
There could be significant impacts on the Canadian streaming market as well. Much of the HBO content available in Canada is on Bell’s Crave platform, since HBO’s streaming service isn’t available in Canada. Bell has said Warner Bros. programming will stay on Crave “for the foreseeable future,” but didn’t clarify how long its current licensing deal will last.
Moreover, there are political concerns with the merger. Paramount Skydance owner David Ellison and his father, Oracle-owner Larry Ellison have close ties to U.S. President Donald Trump.
We’ve already seen Ellison direct changes to benefit Trump, including picking political commentator Bari Weiss as editor-in-chief of CBS News and firing journalists at 60 Minutes. Ellison reportedly promised Trump there would similar changes to CNN should the deal go through. Elsewhere, Paramount reportedly greenlit projects like Rush Hour 4 just to please Trump.
Beyond the Ellisons, the Paramount bid’s Saudi Arabia backing drew criticism, given the Saudi government infamously ordered the murder of Washington Post journalist Jamal Khashoggi after he criticized the regime. In a similar vein, Saudi Arabia is backing a Trump-linked takeover of Electronic Arts (EA), all part of a broader push to rebrand the country’s image.

articles.title: F1’s real business: why Qatar pays $55 million a year to host a race
articles.text:
F1’s real business: why Qatar pays $55 million a year to host a race
Formula 1 increasingly operates like a global media business, with governments paying huge premiums for the tourism, visibility and influence delivered by a Grand Prix.
Watch a Formula 1 race and the business looks obvious: fans in the grandstands, cars on track, a winner on the podium. But the ticket revenue from that grandstand almost entirely bypasses Formula 1 itself. It goes to the local race promoter. What F1's parent company, Liberty Media, actually collects is something most fans never think about: a hosting fee, paid by the circuit or, increasingly, by the national government behind it, just for the right to be on the calendar at all.
A revenue model with no single centre of gravity
F1's 2025 financials break down into four uneven but complementary pillars. According to Liberty Media's full-year results, media rights fees accounted for 31.3% of total F1 revenue, race promotion (hosting) fees for 26.7%, sponsorship for 21.7%, and everything else (hospitality, freight, licensing, F1 TV) for 20.3%. No single stream dominates, which is precisely what makes the model so resilient.
Total revenue hit a record $3.87 billion in 2025, a 14% jump on the year before. Revenue has now risen for five consecutive seasons, and setting aside the pandemic-disrupted 2020 campaign, when the calendar was gutted, it has grown virtually every year since Liberty Media bought the sport from a CVC Capital Partners-led consortium in 2017.
The hosting-fee line tells the growth story in miniature. In 2017, the year after Liberty took over, promoter fees were worth $503 million, roughly 34% of the sport's primary revenue. Eight years later that single line item had grown to $824 million. Its share of the pie actually shrank slightly over that period, a sign not that hosting fees stalled, but of just how much bigger the whole business became around them.
Why some countries pay several times more than others to host the same 20 cars
The gap between what different circuits pay is where this gets genuinely strange. Monaco, one of the oldest and most prestigious races on the calendar, first run in 1929, has long paid around $20 million a year, the lowest fee anywhere on the grid. Liberty pushed hard on its renewal, and Monaco is now locked in through 2035. Reporting suggests the new fee climbed substantially, though the exact figure hasn't been officially disclosed.
Compare that to Qatar, Saudi Arabia, and Azerbaijan, each paying an estimated $55 to $57 million a year. Qatar's Losail circuit committed to a 10-year deal worth $550 million in total, meaning a race that joined the calendar in 2021 pays close to three times what the sport's crown jewel does. Saudi Arabia's overall F1 outlay, combining its hosting fee with Aramco's global sponsorship, is widely estimated to exceed $100 million a year, though the components aren't publicly itemised.
Traditional European circuits like Silverstone, Monza, and Spa lean heavily on ticket sales and commercial partnerships to cover their fees, largely funding themselves. Gulf-state races operate on a fundamentally different model: their hosting fees are paid or substantially subsidised directly by national governments, not by ticket revenue or local promoters trying to break even.
Some analysts and commentators have described this as a form of nation-branding or "sportswashing," using a marquee global sporting event to shape international perception. Hosting governments typically frame it differently, as tourism investment and economic development rather than image management. Both readings can point to the same balance sheet.
What happens when the fee, not the fanbase, drives the calendar
The clearest proof that hosting economics now shape F1's calendar came in 2026, when the Bahrain and Saudi Arabian Grands Prix were cancelled amid armed conflict in the Middle East. Both countries were among the Gulf states struck during the fighting that followed US-Israeli airstrikes on Iran. F1 confirmed the cancellations rather than reschedule, cutting the season from 24 races to 22.
According to a Guggenheim analyst note, those two races together represent roughly $115 million in hosting fees, about 14% of F1's entire promoter-fee income. And yet the sport's core financial structure barely flinched. Broadcast rights, sponsorship deals, and prize distribution, the contracts that actually anchor the business, don't reset or shrink just because one or two races vanish from the calendar. The races themselves have become closer to interchangeable inputs into a much larger revenue machine.
Why this matters beyond motorsport
F1's real business isn't cars going fast, and it was never really about ticket sales either. It's a media and sponsorship company that happens to stage races, financed increasingly by governments willing to pay enormous premiums for the global visibility a Grand Prix weekend delivers.
The chequered flag makes for great television. But the money changes hands long before any car reaches the grid, in contracts signed between Liberty Media and national treasuries that have decided hosting Formula 1 is worth paying for, whatever happens on track.

articles.title: Canicule : votre déshumidificateur peut-il vous aider à supporter la chaleur ?
articles.text:
Canicule : votre déshumidificateur peut-il vous aider à supporter la chaleur ?
Un coup de secLorsque la température grimpe, l'humidité peut rendre l'air encore plus difficile à supporter. Un déshumidificateur permet alors d'améliorer le confort, mais seulement dans certaines conditions. Et sans jamais remplacer un climatiseur.
Ventilateur, climatiseur, volets fermés... Le déshumidificateur ne figure pas souvent parmi les appareils auxquels on pense pendant une vague de chaleur. Pourtant, le fabricant Wood's, qui nous avait proposer de tester son modèle MDX20P, estime qu'il pourrait jouer un rôle lorsque les températures élevées s'accompagnent d'une forte humidité.
Wood's MDX20P
La marque prend pour exemple une température de 32 °C associée à 70 % d'humidité. D'après le calculateur du National Weather Service américain, cette combinaison correspond effectivement à un indice de chaleur proche de 41 °C. Une valeur indicative, puisque cet outil a d'abord été conçu pour évaluer le ressenti à l'extérieur, à l'ombre et avec peu de vent.
Quand la transpiration ne suffit plus
Cette sensation de chaleur plus intense s'explique par le fonctionnement de notre organisme. Pour se refroidir, le corps produit de la transpiration, dont l'évaporation évacue une partie de la chaleur. Lorsque l'air est déjà chargé en vapeur d'eau, cette évaporation devient moins efficace. Nous transpirons toujours, mais avec un résultat nettement moins rafraîchissant.
En retirant une partie de l'humidité présente dans l'air, un déshumidificateur peut donc rendre une pièce moins étouffante et faciliter l'évaporation de la transpiration. L'intérêt sera perceptible dans un logement affichant une hygrométrie supérieure à 60 %, lorsque les épisodes de chaleur s'accompagnent d'un air lourd. Wood's conseille une plage de 40 à 60 %.
Avant de remettre en service son déshumidificateur en pleine canicule, mieux vaut donc commencer par regarder un appareil qui affiche le taux d'humidité, comme une station météo. Si l'humidité se situe déjà autour de 40 ou 50 %, son fonctionnement apportera peu de confort supplémentaire.
SwitchBot Station Météo Intelligente
Attention toutefois, un déshumidificateur ne refroidit pas la pièce. Les modèles à compresseur aspirent l'air humide, condensent l'eau qu'il contient, puis rejettent un air plus sec, mais aussi légèrement plus chaud. À cela s'ajoutent leur consommation électrique et leur niveau sonore. Dans une pièce déjà chaude et relativement sèche, le remède pourrait ainsi devenir plus pénible que le mal.
Une forte humidité augmente également le travail demandé à un climatiseur, qui doit à la fois refroidir et assécher l'air. Une déshumidification séparée peut l'aider dans certains logements très humides, mais elle implique de faire fonctionner deux appareils.
Le déshumidificateur peut finalement apporter un peu de répit lorsque la chaleur devient moite et collante. Il ne fera toutefois pas baisser le thermomètre et ne remplace ni la climatisation ni les précautions indispensables pendant une canicule.

articles.title: Priscillia Choy Sze Mun, experta en células madre: "El ejercicio le indica a los músculos que se limpien y se reinicien"
articles.text:
Los efectos del ejercicio físico para las personas mayores están más que demostrados. Les ayuda a mejorar su salud cardiovascular, mejora la movilidad, reduce las fracturas y, en general, aporta un largo etcétera de beneficios. Es bueno en todas las etapas de la vida, pero cuando nos vamos haciendo mayores se convierte en algo esencial. Sin embargo, a pesar de lo bien estudiado que está esto, hasta hace poco no estaba claro por qué es tan beneficioso. Conocer el motivo es necesario, ya que puede ayudar a exprimir aún más esas ventajas.
Ahora, un equipo de científicos de la Facultad de Medicina Duke-NUS, en colaboración con la Universidad de Cardiff y el Hospital General de Singapur, ha dado un gran paso en este sentido, al descubrir las vías moleculares causantes tanto del deterioro de la salud muscular en edades avanzadas como de los beneficios del ejercicio físico para las personas mayores.
Vías moleculares que se resienten. Este estudio se apoya en investigaciones previas, en las que ya se apuntaba a la posible implicación de la vía mTORC1, implicada en la regulación de la síntesis y eliminación de proteínas musculares. Esta vía debe mantener un equilibrio entre la síntesis de nuevas proteínas y la eliminación de aquellas que están dañadas. Sin embargo, se ha visto que, a medida que nos hacemos mayores, esta vía se desregula, decantando la balanza hacia la síntesis de nuevas proteínas. Las proteínas dañadas que normalmente deberían eliminarse se van acumulando, provocando estrés en las células musculares y dando lugar a una pérdida progresiva de fuerza.
Esta vía, a su vez, está regulada por otra, llamada DEAF 1. Según han visto estos científicos, cuando aumenta la actividad de esta, aumenta la expresión de genes de la vía mTORC1, provocando ese desequilibrio hacia la síntesis de proteínas. Además, lo que vieron estos científicos en experimentos con moscas de la fruta y ratones es que la actividad de DEAF 1 está regulada por la actividad de un grupo de proteínas que también existen en humanos: FOXOs. Las mantienen a raya. El problema es que la actividad de FOXO disminuye con la edad, por lo que se da rienda suelta a DEAF 1 y, con ello, al desequilibrio en la síntesis y eliminación de proteínas musculares.
El papel del ejercicio físico en personas mayores. En su estudio, estos científicos han visto que el ejercicio físico reactiva las proteínas FOXOs. Por eso, el ejercicio físico en personas mayores ayuda a mantener el equilibrio en la síntesis y eliminación de proteínas musculares, mejorando la masa muscular y aumentando los beneficios asociados a ella.
También células madre. DEAF 1 no influye en los músculos solamente mediante la desregulación de la síntesis y eliminación de proteínas. También se relaciona con la síntesis de células madre musculares. Esta, normalmente, disminuye con la edad. Por eso, encontrar formas de mantener unos buenos niveles de actividad es clave. El ejercicio físico en personas mayores ayuda también en ese sentido.
No es igual para todo el mundo. En su estudio, estos científicos han visto que, por desgracia, el ejercicio físico no parece ser siempre una buena herramienta en solitario. Hay personas para las que es suficiente, mientras que otras deben recurrir a estrategias adicionales para mejorar su salud. Este es el camino por el que deben seguir estudiando.
No solo para personas mayores. Este estudio no va dirigido solo a estudiar los beneficios del ejercicio físico en personas mayores. Sus autores creen que también puede ser útil para pacientes que hayan perdido masa muscular por recuperarse de una cirugía, una caída o enfermedades como el cáncer. Sea como sea, la clave inicial está en comprender los mecanismos que merman la salud muscular de personas mayores.
Según una de las autoras del estudio, Priscillia Choy Sze Mun, “el ejercicio físico dice a los músculos que se limpien y se reinicien”. Lógicamente, habrá que estudiar más. Para empezar, habría que comprobar que, por mucho que se compartan los mecanismos, lo que se ha visto en ratones es extrapolable a humanos. De ser así, tendríamos un conocimiento clave para mejorar los programas de ejercicio físico para personas mayores. El conocimiento es poder y, en ciencia, saber los porqués de las cosas es poderosísimo.

articles.title: Google reportedly developing ‘Frozen v2’ AI chip optimized for Gemini models - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Google reportedly developing ‘Frozen v2’ AI chip optimized for Gemini models
Google LLC is reportedly developing a new chip optimized to run its Gemini series of artificial intelligence models.
Sources told The Information today that the processor is codenamed “Frozen v2.” According to the publication, it’s expected to provide between six and 10 times better performance per watt than the search giant’s current silicon. Shares of Google parent Alphabet Inc. rose 1.5% on the report.
Off-the-shelf chips often contain components that customers don’t need. If an AI startup buys a graphics card that includes both inference and rendering cores, it may end up leaving the latter modules idle. That can lead to inefficiencies in AI projects.
Designing a custom chip addresses the challenge. A company can leave out circuits that aren’t needed for its workloads and thereby lower manufacturing costs. Alternatively, it can replace the unnecessary circuits with cores optimized for its use case.
Google has long offered custom AI chips called TPUs through its public cloud. The two newest entries in the lineup, the TPU 8t and TPUi, are optimized for training and inference, respectively. According to today’s report, Google plans to take that customization a step further by optimizing its upcoming Frozen v2 chip for its Gemini models’ architecture.
The significant efficiency gains that the company reportedly expects to unlock will be achieved through multiple routes. In particular, the company hopes that Frozen v2 will reduce the number of calculations needed to run Gemini. It also will reportedly reduce data movement.
Data movement is an issue when a neural network can’t fit into a graphics card’s onboard memory. When that happens, neural network elements are stored in off-chip storage. The graphics card must regularly move those elements from the off-chip storage to its logic circuits and vice versa, which slows down processing.
Google could address that bottleneck by equipping Frozen v2 with enough memory to run Gemini fully on-chip. Such a design would remove the need to move data to and from off-chip RAM.
The fact that Frozen v2 is expected to reduce the number of calculations needed to run Gemini suggests that it will also support a form of operator fusion. That’s a widely used technique for speeding up AI models. It works by combining several calculations into a single computation that can be completed faster.
Google runs its TPUs in clusters that contain multiple custom components. The TPU 8i, for example, relies on custom devices called optical circuit switches to manage the flow of data. Google will presumably make Frozen v2 compatible with those components to avoid the need for major cluster redesigns.
The company reportedly hopes to start rolling out the chip to its data centers in 2028.

articles.title: Pixel 6 et 6 Pro : Google annonce la fin du support logiciel
articles.text:
Lancée par Google pour les bêta-testeurs, la première version bêta d’Android 17 QPR2 est une première étape avec la mise à jour stable prévue pour le quatrième trimestre 2026. Comme il s’agit du déploiement public qui aura lieu après le mois d’octobre, les Pixel 6 et 6 Pro ne seront à cette date plus pris en charge. La liste des appareils Pixel compatibles est de plus en plus restreinte, une première depuis près de trois ans.
Une date limite connue depuis longtemps
Sortis initialement le 19 octobre 2021 et commercialisés le 28 octobre de la même année, les deux smartphones devaient à l’origine s’arrêter à Android 15. Google s’engageait alors sur seulement trois ans de mises à jour de son OS. L’arrivée des Pixel 8 et de leur promesse de suivi sur sept ans a poussé la firme de Mountain View à revoir ses plans, accordant une extension à cinq ans aux Pixel 6 et Pixel 7.
Bien que la version QPR1 (avec le Feature Drop de septembre) arrive juste avant le cinquième anniversaire des Pixel 6, la bêta QPR2 arrivera après. Le Pixel 6a profite pour l’instant d’un répit en étant intégré au programme bêta. Il devrait recevoir Android 18 avant d’atteindre sa date limite fixée au 21 juillet 2027. Pour les autres, la fin du support logiciel n’est donc pas une surprise.
Une liste d’appareils de plus en plus resserrée
Le Google Pixel 5 a été écarté avec Android 14 QPR1 Beta 1 en septembre 2023. De leur côté, les utilisateurs de Pixel 6 pourront conserver leur appareil, même si leur appareil n’est plus officiellement mis à jour. On constate cependant que le catalogue des smartphones Google pris en charge est de moins en moins important.
À lire : Pixel 11 Pro Fold : une fuite dévoile l’une des versions avant l’annonce de Google
Les prochains Pixel concernés par la fin de leur cycle de mise à jour sont évidemment les Pixel 7, 7 Pro, 7a et le Pixel Fold, qui s’apprêtent à subir un sort identique d’ici un an. Seule la série Pixel 8 échappera provisoirement à ce couperet, avec une fin de support en octobre 2030.
